import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis (1000 Cameras)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_colors = {'Full Frame': '#e74c3c', 'APS-C': '#3498db', 'Micro 4/3': '#2ecc71'}
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, c=sensor_colors.get(sensor, '#95a5a6'), s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = sns.color_palette('viridis', len(brand_prices))
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Brand (Top 10 Brands)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for bar, price in zip(bars, brand_prices.values):
    ax2.text(price + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${price:.0f}', 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Body Type Distribution with 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#e74c3c', '#2ecc71'], edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Body Type Distribution with 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', loc='upper right')
ax3.set_xticklabels(ax3.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Evolution of Megapixels Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': ['mean', 'std'],
    'price_usd': 'mean'
}).reset_index()
yearly_stats.columns = ['model_year', 'mp_mean', 'mp_std', 'price_mean']

ax4.fill_between(yearly_stats['model_year'], 
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] - yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] + yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  alpha=0.3, color='#3498db', label='±1 Std Dev')
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mp_mean'], 
         color='#2c3e50', linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Mean Megapixels')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Evolution of Camera Resolution Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
